name: Oyster Soup, No. 2
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Celery salt, marjoram, thyme, mace, or onion (optional)
ingredients.originalText: Celery salt, marjoram, thyme, mace, or onion (optional)

instructions.text: Scald one gallon of oysters in their own liquor
Add one quart of rich milk to the liquor and bring to a boil
Skim out the oysters and set aside
Mix the yolks of four eggs, two tablespoonfuls of butter, and one tablespoonful of flour well together
Add the milk first, then after beating the eggs, add a little of the hot liquor to them gradually
Stir them rapidly into the soup
Add the butter and seasoning of your choice (celery salt, marjoram, thyme, mace, or onion)
Season to taste with pepper and salt with caution

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Scald one gallon of oysters in their own liquor
2. Add one quart of rich milk to the liquor and bring to a boil
3. Skim out the oysters and set aside
4. Mix the yolks of four eggs, two tablespoonfuls of butter, and one tablespoonful of flour well together
5. Add the milk first, then after beating the eggs, add a little of the hot liquor to them gradually
6. Stir them rapidly into the soup
7. Add the butter and seasoning of your choice (celery salt, marjoram, thyme, mace, or onion)
8. Season to taste with pepper and salt with caution
